components.description: Unpaid, job-protected family and medical leave of up to 12 weeks in 12 months under the FMLA (HOP 5-4310; Regents' Rule 30201 Sec. 12), for the birth and care of a child, adoption or foster placement, the employee's own serious health condition, or care of a spouse; accrued paid leave must be used concurrently.

components.duration_note: HOP 5-4310 'up to twelve (12) weeks ... during a period of twelve (12) months'; the statute: 'a total of 12 workweeks of leave during any 12-month period' (29 U.S.C. 2612(a)(1)). Military caregiver leave (26 weeks) is an FMLA provision not related to a birth. U8: HOP 5-4330 Parental Leave (2018_00; Regents' Rule 30201 Sec. 6; Texas Government Code 661.913) gives up to 12 weeks of unpaid parental leave, beginning at the birth or placement, to employees who are not eligible for FML (faculty appointed at least 50% for at least 4 1/2 months); accrued annual and sick leave must be used, then leave without pay; time on it counts toward FML once the employee becomes eligible. The Provost page adds that where both parents are university employees their combined parental leave entitlement is 12 weeks. The member described (two years of service) is FML-eligible, so this path is recorded here, not as a component.

components.institution_label: Extension of the Tenure Track Probationary Period
components.description: On written request, a one-academic-year extension of the tenure-track probationary period for personal circumstances (an open list including the faculty member's illness and being the principal caregiver of a preschool child), decided by the Provost; at most two years in total.
components.eligible_parent_wording: the principal caregiver of a preschool child; disability or illness of the faculty member
components.caregiver_condition_wording: status of the faculty member as the principal caregiver of a preschool child
components.duration_note: One academic year per request; a second year in exceptional circumstances; at most two academic years in total.
components.notice: request no later than the end of the spring semester before the sixth year of probationary service

faculty_group: A tenure track faculty member who determines that certain personal circumstances may impede his or her progress toward achieving demonstration of eligibility for recommendation of the award of tenure may make a written request for extension of the probationary period specifying the reasons for the requested extension.
eligible_parent: Personal circumstances that may justify the extension include, but are not restricted to: disability or illness of the faculty member; status of the faculty member as the principal caregiver of a preschool child; or, status of the faculty member as a principal caregiver of a disabled, elderly, or ill member of the family of the faculty member.

notes: Reference date 2018-04-17. HOP pages are 2019 Wayback captures of policies issued 1997-2005 (version notes: no captures 2016-10 to 2019-07; text in force on the reference date); Provost and HR pages are 2017 captures; Regents' Rules 30201 (amended 2017-03-06) and 31007 (amended 2016-02-10) are 2017 captures. All are read as in force on the reference date. HOP 2-2210 carries a Workday review banner from the 2019 capture.

Governing documents: the Handbook of Operating Procedures (HOP 5-4310 FML, 5-4330 Parental Leave, 5-4210 Sick Leave, 2-2210 Faculty Leaves, 2-2240 Modified Instructional Duties, 2-2020 probationary extension) and UT System Regents' Rules 30201 and 31007. Summaries: the Provost Leaves & Related Policies and Life & Work pages, and the HR FMLA page. HOP 5-4610 (staff leave without pay) states it does not apply to faculty (c5).

No employer-paid parental leave exists in the sources. A birth parent's pay comes only from accrued sick leave (usually up to 6 weeks, or 8 after a cesarean, per the HR page), then other accrued leave, then the sick leave pool for catastrophic conditions; the remainder of FML is unpaid.

U8: HOP 5-4330 Parental Leave (up to 12 weeks unpaid, from the birth or placement, for employees not eligible for FML; Texas Government Code 661.913; Regents' Rule 30201 Sec. 6) is recorded in c1's duration_note, not as a component, because the member described (two years of service) is FML-eligible. The Provost page's 'Where both parents are employed by the university, their total combined parental leave entitlement is 12 weeks' refers to this parental leave.

Tenure clock: HOP 2-2020 says an extension is 'never automatic' and is decided by the Provost (c7, discretionary, general_purpose under U1's open list). The Provost summary (2017) says it is 'automatic for reasons of childbirth and/or adoption upon notification' (c8, flagged summary_only and conflicting_sources); the governing HOP decides (source precedence).

Birth parent chain: FML 12 weeks (c1), with accrued sick leave paid within it (c2, own balance, usually 6/8 weeks) and the sick leave pool after the balance (c3, discretionary) -> faculty leave without pay up to one academic year after FML expires (c4, general purpose, discretionary). Modified instructional duties, one semester of teaching relief for a principal caregiver of a pre-school child (c6, discretionary), is unlinked: the documents state no order relative to the leave, and it is not intended where sick leave applies.

Non-birth parent chain: FML 12 weeks (c1), with sick leave usable within it only to care for the spouse recovering from childbirth or an ill child (c2) -> faculty leave without pay (c4, general purpose). Modified instructional duties (c6) as for the birth parent, unlinked.

Documents cited but not saved: HOP 5-4220 Sick Leave Pool; HOP 5-4320 Foster Parent Leave; HOP 2-2240's source Regents' Rule 31006 Academic Workload Requirements; the Provost's Leave_Related_Policies.pdf summary table; the Faculty Request for Leave form; HOP 5-4430 Military Leave; Regents' Rules 30103, 31001, 31002; Texas Government Code 661.912, 661.913, 661.909, 661.201-206, 661.033-034, 659.016(e), 659.085. Only those bearing on parental provisions are flagged on components.
Long-term disability insurance is mentioned once on the HR FMLA page, as a cost the employee pays during FML; no terms are stated, so it is not coded.
No saved document refers to a collective agreement.
